extracted_claims.text: Under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act) Article 113, the general date of application of the Regulation is 2 August 2026, and the obligations for high-risk AI systems under Sections 1-3 of Chapter III (which includes Annex III systems) were originally set to apply from that date.

The European Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI proposal, COM(2025)836, was put forward because delayed availability of standards, common specifications, guidance, and national competent authorities jeopardized the feasibility of the 2 August 2026 application date for high-risk obligations.

Co-legislators reached a trilogue agreement on the Digital Omnibus on AI on 7 May 2026, setting fixed deadlines for high-risk obligations: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone Annex III high-risk AI systems and 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI systems embedded in Annex I regulated products.

The Council of the European Union gave final approval to the Digital Omnibus simplification package on 29 June 2026, confirming the postponement of the Annex III high-risk deadline from 2 August 2026 to 2 December 2027, and the Annex I embedded-product deadline from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028.
The Digital Omnibus on AI entered into force on 27 July 2026.
As adopted, the applicable deadline for obligations on stand-alone high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III is now 2 December 2027, superseding the original 2 August 2026 date in the AI Act.
The deadline for high-risk AI systems that are safety components of Annex I regulated products was moved from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028.

The Commission's original proposal would have tied application of the high-risk rules to a Commission Decision confirming completion of standards and guidance, with a backstop of 2 December 2027 (Annex III) and 2 August 2028 (Annex I) if no such Decision was made.

The final agreed Digital Omnibus text dropped the standards-readiness-check mechanism, making 2 December 2027 and 2 August 2028 fixed calendar dates rather than conditions dependent on regulatory readiness.

Despite the postponement of Annex III high-risk obligations, other AI Act obligations remain on the original 2 August 2026 schedule, including Article 5 prohibitions, GPAI obligations, and transparency duties (e.g., chatbot disclosure, Article 50).
Some sources state that Annex III high-risk obligations apply, or became enforceable, from 2 August 2026, without reference to the Digital Omnibus postponement.
A Council document (LIMITE) indicates that at least one Member State (Austria) was still analyzing the Digital Omnibus and the Digital Omnibus on AI and had raised a scrutiny reservation.

It is unclear whether the sources stating 2 August 2026 for Annex III obligations (6, 7, 8, 16) were published before the Digital Omnibus on AI was finalized, since none of them carry publication dates, making it impossible to definitively label them as outdated versus simply incorrect.

The exact sequence and dates of adoption steps (trilogue agreement 7 May 2026, Council approval 29 June 2026, entry into force 27 July 2026) are reported in different sources without a single source confirming all three, leaving the full legislative timeline only partially corroborated.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI System Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the application date for obligations governing high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 113](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-113)). However, through the Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI proposal and subsequent trilogue negotiations, this deadline has been postponed to **2 December 2027** for stand-alone Annex III systems, with a separate deadline of 2 August 2028 for high-risk AI systems embedded in Annex I regulated products ([Europarl Legislative Train](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/package-digital-package/file-digital-omnibus-on-ai); [Gibson Dunn](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes)) (high confidence). Despite this shift, significant uncertainty remains regarding the precise legislative status and final legal text of the postponement.

## Key Findings

### Original Legal Deadline
Under Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (the AI Act), Article 113 set the general date of application at 2 August 2026, which included the Chapter III, Sections 1–3 obligations covering Annex III high-risk systems ([AI Act Service Desk, Article 113](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-113); [AI Act Service Desk Timeline](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/timeline/timeline-implementation-eu-ai-act)) (high confidence).

### Rationale for Delay
The European Commission's Digital Omnibus on AI proposal, COM(2025)836, was introduced because delays in the availability of harmonized standards, common specifications, guidance documents, and the designation of national competent authorities jeopardized the feasibility of meeting the original 2 August 2026 deadline ([EUR-Lex COM(2025)836](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A52025PC0836); [Winston Taylor](https://www.winstontaylor.com/insights/ai-act-rules-on-high-risk-ai-delayed-as-ai-digital-omnibus-agreed)) (high confidence). The Commission's original proposal would have tied application to a Commission Decision confirming regulatory readiness, with a 2 December 2027/2 August 2028 backstop if no such Decision issued (low confidence) ([Winston Taylor](https://www.winstontaylor.com/insights/ai-act-rules-on-high-risk-ai-delayed-as-ai-digital-omnibus-agreed)).

### Negotiated and Adopted Postponement
Co-legislators reportedly reached a trilogue agreement on 7 May 2026, fixing new deadlines: 2 December 2027 for stand-alone Annex III systems and 2 August 2028 for Annex I-embedded systems (medium confidence) ([Europarl Legislative Train](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/legislative-train/package-digital-package/file-digital-omnibus-on-ai)). As adopted, multiple sources confirm 2 December 2027 as the applicable deadline for stand-alone Annex III obligations, superseding the original date (high confidence) ([Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2); [Gibson Dunn](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes)). Similarly, the Annex I embedded-product deadline was moved from 2 August 2027 to 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([Cloud Security Alliance Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-omnibus-vii-deadline-delay-20260)). One source claims the Council gave final approval on 29 June 2026 and another states the Digital Omnibus entered into force on 27 July 2026, though neither claim is independently corroborated across multiple sources (low confidence) ([CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-omnibus-vii-deadline-delay-20260); [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)). The final agreed text reportedly dropped the standards-readiness-check mechanism in favor of fixed calendar dates (low confidence) ([CloseIT](https://www.closeit.co/post/eu-ai-act-digital-omnibus-what-changed)).

### Obligations Unaffected by the Delay
Other AI Act obligations remain on the original 2 August 2026 schedule, including Article 5 prohibited practices, GPAI model obligations, and transparency duties such as chatbot disclosure under Article 50 (low confidence) ([CloseIT](https://www.closeit.co/post/eu-ai-act-digital-omnibus-what-changed); [Praxikon](https://www.praxikon.com/en/posts/digital-omnibus-high-risk-postponement-december-2027)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Several sources state that Annex III obligations apply or became enforceable from 2 August 2026 without any reference to the Digital Omnibus postponement, directly conflicting with sources describing the 2 December 2027 deadline (high confidence claim vs. high confidence claim) ([AIactIndex](https://aiactindex.eu/eu-ai-act/high-risk-systems); [AnnexOps](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)). Given the absence of publication dates, it is plausible the 2 August 2026 sources predate the Omnibus finalization, but this cannot be confirmed.

A Council LIMITE document indicates Austria had raised a scrutiny reservation and was still analyzing the Digital Omnibus on AI (medium confidence), which appears inconsistent with claims that the Council gave final approval on 29 June 2026 (low confidence, 0.12) ([Council LIMITE document](https://data.consilium.europa.eu/doc/document/WK-17679-2025-INIT/en/pdf); [CSA Labs](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-eu-ai-act-omnibus-vii-deadline-delay-20260)). It is unclear whether the reservation predates or postdates the reported approval.

Several claims regarding the exact legislative sequence (trilogue date, Council approval, entry into force) carry low confidence scores (0.12–0.17) and should be treated cautiously pending stronger corroboration.

## Knowledge Gaps
The precise Official Journal citation and final adopted legal text of the Digital Omnibus on AI remain unconfirmed. It is unclear whether sources citing the original 2 August 2026 deadline are simply outdated or substantively incorrect. No single source corroborates the full sequence of trilogue agreement, Council approval, and entry into force. Transitional provisions for Annex III systems already on the market are not detailed. Finally, the resolution status of Austria's scrutiny reservation and its effect on the final text remains unknown.
